outcomes.text: Name the main Greek gods and their Roman equivalents, with their responsibilities and symbols.
Describe how the gods are typically shown in Greek and Roman art.
Retell the myth of Heracles as founder of the Olympic games.
Describe the 12 Labours as shown on the Temple of Zeus at Olympia and in the Homeric Hymn to Heracles.
Retell Hercules and Cacus and explain Hercules as protector of Rome.
Retell the battles with Achelous and Nessus and the death of Hercules in Ovid.
Describe temple layout: altar position, naos or cella and cult statue, and how worshippers used it.
Describe the Parthenon and Temple of Zeus at Olympia.
Explain the roles of the hiereus, hiereia and mantis, and the purpose and practice of animal sacrifice.
Describe the Temple of Fortuna Virilis and the Pantheon.
Explain the roles of the Pontiffs, Pontifex Maximus, Augurs and Vestal Virgins.
Explain Roman animal sacrifice and the haruspex.

topics.title: Myth and the City: Foundation Stories

outcomes.text: Retell the naming of Athens by Poseidon and Athena and what it meant to the city.
Retell the adventures of Theseus as shown on the Theseus Kylix.
Retell Aeneas' leadership of the Trojans, settlement in Italy and the line of kings from Alba Longa.
Retell the founding of Rome by Romulus and Remus.
Compare Theseus and Romulus using Plutarch's Lives.
Describe the City Dionysia and Great Panathenaia: origins, officials, sacrifice, programme and participants.
Describe the Lupercalia and Saturnalia: origins, officials, sacrifice, programme and participants.

subtopics.title: Myth as a symbol of power

outcomes.text: Explain how the Centauromachy on the Parthenon and Amazonomachy on the Bassae frieze show power.
Explain how the Prima Porta of Augustus and the Ara Pacis use myth to show power, and why where they stood matters.
Describe Greek preparation of the body (prothesis), funeral procession (ekphora), burial with stelai, and festivals for the dead such as the Genesia.
Describe Roman preparation of the body, funeral clubs, procession, burial, and festivals for the dead such as Parentalia and Lemuria.
Retell Persephone and Demeter in the Homeric Hymn to Demeter, with characters and portrayal of the underworld.
Retell Orpheus and Eurydice in Ovid's Metamorphoses 10, with characters and portrayal of the underworld.
Compare how the Greek and Roman texts depict and reflect ancient culture.
Retell the stories of Pandora and Helen of Troy and explain what they say about Greek views of women and virtue.
Retell the Sabine Women, Tarpeia and Lucretia and explain what they say about Roman views of women and virtue.

subtopics.title: Young women in Athens and Sparta

outcomes.text: Describe Athenian education at home for marriage and typical wedding rituals.
Describe the Spartan system of education and marriage.
Describe Roman girls' education at home and evidence of academic education for some.
Explain Roman marriage types coemptio, confarreatio and usus, and cum manu versus sine manu.
Explain the kyria, Athenian ideas of wifely virtue, and Athenian domestic slaves.
Describe the experience of a Spartan wife and mother.
Explain the matrona, Roman ideas of wifely virtue, legal rights, property, divorce and adultery.
Describe the duties of Roman domestic slaves.
Explain roles, laws and portrayal of pornai and hetairai, including at a symposium.
Describe Neaira and Aspasia.
Explain roles, laws and portrayal of the meretrix and lena.
Describe Clodia, her possible identification as 'Lesbia', and Cytheris/Lycoris.
Describe priestesses and prophetesses including the Pythia.
Explain women's roles in state cult: Panathenaia, Thesmophoria and worship of Dionysus, and in mourning rituals.
Describe priestesses: the Vestal Virgins' rights, responsibilities and punishment, and the Flaminica Dialis.
Describe prophetesses including the Sibyl.
Explain women's roles in state cult: Bona Dea, Patricia Pudicitia and Plebeia Pudicitia.
Explain the Athenian Assembly and the exclusion of women.
Describe Aristophanes' Assemblywomen and the trial of Agnodice.
Explain the Roman Senate and the exclusion of women.
Retell the repeal of the Oppian Law, and Sempronia in the Catilinarian Conspiracy.
Describe Penthesilea and the Amazons in Greek art and literature.
Describe Camilla in Virgil's Aeneid.
Explain what these maiden warriors tell us about real women's positions.
Retell Medea's story and its Athenian presentation, from meeting Jason to escaping to Athens.
Retell Cleopatra VII's Roman presentation: love affairs with Caesar and Antony, Actium, and political and military threat.
Explain why foreign powerful women seemed dangerous to ancient audiences.
Date the Mycenaean age and explain the importance of Mycenae, Tiryns and Troy.
Describe the layout and structures of Mycenae and Tiryns, including the Lion Gate, Cyclopean walls and cistern.
Evaluate evidence for and against Troy VI and Troy VIIa being Homer's Troy.

topics.title: Culture: Life in the Mycenaean age

outcomes.text: Describe a typical palace complex, the megaron, and the functions of palaces.
Describe evidence for hunting, armour and weapons, chariots, clothing and trade.
Explain how the Linear B tablets were preserved, what they record and why they matter.
Describe fresco techniques, colours and typical designs.
Describe jewellery techniques and materials: metalwork, amber and glass.
Describe how decorative objects were made: storage and drinking vessels, figures and figurines, votive offerings and ivory carving.
Describe shaft graves, cist graves, and tholos and chamber tombs.
Explain the use of funerary objects.
Describe the contents of Grave Circle A and Grave Circle B at Mycenae.
Explain how the Odyssey may have been composed and performed, and what makes it an epic.
Explain narrative techniques: similes, epithets and formulae.
Explain xenia, guest-friendship.
Explain deceit and trickery, and civilisation versus barbarism of places and characters.
Explain revenge and justice, nostos and fate.
Assess Odysseus as leader, husband and father.
Assess him as warrior and hero, and his intelligence and oratory.
Explain his relationship with Athena and the role of the gods.

topics.title: Literature: The portrayal of key characters

outcomes.text: Describe the portrayal of the suitors and Odysseus' crew.
Describe Polyphemus as monster and keeper of livestock, and Circe as witch and host.
Describe Penelope as host, wife and queen, and Telemachus as son and hero.
Assess the loyalty or disloyalty of Odysseus' slaves.
Describe the design of insulae (apartment blocks).
Describe the layout and decoration of a typical Pompeian atrium-style domus.
Compare living conditions of the rich and the poor.

topics.title: Culture: The Roman Home and Family

outcomes.text: Explain the paterfamilias, his rights and duties.
Explain patrons and clients.
Explain the roles of the litterator, grammaticus and rhetor, subjects taught and preparation for society.
Describe school equipment: stilus, wax tablet, pen, ink and papyrus.
Describe the cena: organisation, guests, entertainment and purposes.
Explain citizens and citizenship.
Compare senators and equites: property qualifications, privileges, duties and roles.
Explain becoming a slave and the legal position of slaves.
Describe skilled and unskilled jobs of domestic and public slaves.
Explain ways of obtaining freedom and limits on freedmen and freedwomen.
Describe amphitheatre design including the Colosseum, and types of shows.
Explain sponsorship of games, and gladiators' status, training and types.
Explain audience involvement.
Describe the design of the Circus Maximus.
Explain teams, colours, charioteers, horses and their status, and public attitudes and involvement.
Describe theatre design, sets, costumes and masks.
Describe Roman comedy and stock characters, mime and pantomime.
Explain the reputation and social standing of actors and actresses.
Explain why people used bath complexes.
Describe bath design, types of bath and activities including the palaestra.
Explain the origins and purposes of satire.
Compare the style of Horace as the smiling satirist and Juvenal as the angry satirist.
Explain the nature and purpose of Petronius' Satyricon.
Explain narrative and descriptive techniques, humour, exaggeration and choice of themes.
Explain Pliny's letters as personal commentary on Roman life, his language and purpose.
Explain how Pliny reflects his social position and the image he projects.

subtopics.title: Life in the city in literature

outcomes.text: Explain how the authors depict dangers of city life, and life for rich and poor.
Explain how the authors depict leisure, entertainment, food and dinner parties.
Explain how the authors depict slaves and masters, patrons and clients, and women and men.

topics.title: Culture: Sparta at War in the 5th century

outcomes.text: Explain Spartan society's structure and its influence on the military.
Describe training and recruitment, including the agoge and syssitia.
Describe equipment, tactics and formation, and army command including perioeci and helots.
Explain the idealisation of war in Sparta.
Retell key events and individuals at Thermopylae: Xerxes, Demaratus, Leonidas, Ephialtes and Dienekes.
Explain the battle's significance and how it was commemorated.

topics.title: Culture: Athens at War in the 5th century

outcomes.text: Explain how the army and navy were paid for, recruited and trained.
Describe equipment, tactics and formations on land and sea.
Explain the structure and command of the forces and the military's impact on Athenian politics and society.
Retell key events and individuals at Salamis: Themistocles, Xerxes and Artemisia.
Explain the battle's significance and how it was commemorated.

topics.title: Culture: The Roman Military in the Imperial Period

outcomes.text: Explain how the Roman army and navy were paid for, recruited and trained.
Describe legion organisation, command and the layout of a legionary fortress.
Describe equipment, tactics and formations of the army and navy.
Retell key events and individuals at Actium: Octavian, Agrippa, Antony and Cleopatra.
Explain its significance and how the Romans commemorated it.
Explain the reasons for the war and its presentation in material sources.
Explain the image of Trajan as emperor, the pursuit of military glory, and the victims of warfare.
Describe the genres and authors of the set texts, their composition and aims.
Explain speeches, similes and imagery, epithets, emotive language and the role of the divine.
Describe the actions and traits of the main characters and how they are depicted.
Explain interactions and relationships between characters.
Explain the depiction of leaders and soldiers, comrades and enemies, non-combatants and women.
Explain glory, honour and shame, comradeship and freedom.
Explain hubris and arrogance, and love and patriotism.
Explain the horror and glorification of warfare, and fear and courage.
Explain family and ancestors, and military and civilian victims of war.
